column4: The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking and ر ض و/B001 as approval; this verse directly joins spending wealth with seeking Allah's pleasure and pictures that intention as a garden on high ground, adding a cultivated image to the section's giving.
The source section's wording ابتغاء وجه ربه is directly matched by giving to kin, poor, and traveler for those who desire Allah's face; the verse makes face-seeking a motive for concrete generosity.
The source section joins seeking God's face with giving; this verse contrasts wealth meant to multiply through usury with charity given seeking Allah's face, whose increase is with Him.

The source section says the giver expects no human recompense; this verse describes spending without following it with reminders or injury, protecting the recipient from being made indebted to the giver.

The source section rejects seeking repayment or gratitude from recipients; this verse says kind speech and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury, sharpening the ethical form of giving.
The source section's giver seeks Allah's face alone; this verse warns that charity done to be seen by people and followed by reminders can be nullified, a specific reversal of that intention.
The source section says وجه can stand for the person himself; here the speaker says his prayer, worship, life, and death belong to Allah, making whole-person dedication explicit.
The source section describes seeking as effortful and ends with the seeker content; this verse speaks of one who desires the Hereafter and strives for it as a believer, whose effort is appreciated.

The source section glosses ب غ ي/B001 as seeking and says ابتغاء entails effort; this ayah states that a person has only what he strives for, making the effort itself the basis of the eventual outcome.
The source section describes exertion in seeking; following 53:39's account of striving, this ayah says the effort will be seen, adding its disclosure before recompense in 53:41.
The source section ends with the seeker's future contentment; following 53:39-40, this ayah says the effort will be repaid in full, completing the sequence from striving to outcome.

The source section names ب غ ي/B001 as seeking with effort; this verse commands seeking the Hereafter through what God gave while forbidding seeking corruption, contrasting the proper object of pursuit with a corrupt one.
The source section's face image gives a direction toward God; this verse depicts people blocking paths and seeking to make God's way crooked, a specific reversal of the straight orientation.

The source section sets the sought Lord against turning away; this verse describes people who hinder from God's path, seek to make it crooked, and disbelieve in the Hereafter, joining crooked direction to denial.
The source section says the face turns toward God Himself; this verse forbids prostration to sun or moon and directs worship to their Creator, a clear boundary between a sign and the One sought.

The source section's root ر ض و/B001 describes contentment and approval; after danger, these people follow Allah's pleasure and return with grace and no harm, showing approval as an orienting aim under pressure.

The source section ends with the seeker pleasingly content; here Allah is pleased with believers as they pledge allegiance beneath the tree, connecting divine approval to a concrete act of commitment.
The source section's root ر ض و/B001 names approval; this verse gives the early emigrants, helpers, and their faithful followers the reciprocal reward of Allah's pleasure and their pleasure in Him.

The source section's sought face means God Himself; here Allah says He is pleased with those whose faith and loyalty are firm even against opponents of God and His Messenger, tying approval to allegiance.
The source section quotes those who patiently seek their Lord's face in 13:22; this next ayah names the Gardens of Eden they enter with their righteous kin, continuing that seekers' promised outcome.
The source section links patience with seeking the Lord's face in 13:22; here the angels greet the entrants with peace because of their patience, completing the neighboring account's reward.
The source section says turning away can mean abandoning heed and obedience; this verse describes the one who turns away from remembrance of his Lord and the punishment that follows.

The source section locates the dying denier's conduct in the moment when life reaches the collarbones; this ayah supplies that threshold scene before 75:31-32 name his failure to affirm and his turning away.

The source section says the search ends in meeting the sought Lord; this adjacent death passage says that on that day the drive is to the Lord, giving the dying scene in 75:26 and 75:31-32 its destination.

The source section directs the seeker toward the Lord and says His face remains; this ayah states the contrary preference for the near life, while 87:17 says the Hereafter is better and more enduring.
The source section says the sought face endures; this neighboring ayah calls the Hereafter better and more lasting, completing the contrast with preference for the near life in 87:16.

The source section's root و ل ي/B007 includes turning away by ceasing to heed; this ayah distinguishes people who merely say they hear from those who actually hear, following the command not to turn away while listening in 8:20.

The source section describes turning away as failure to heed and comply; after 8:20-21 warns against that refusal, this ayah commands believers to respond when Allah and the Messenger call them to what gives life.

The source section explains turning away as either bodily withdrawal or abandoning attention; this ayah depicts a person who turns away arrogantly from recited signs as if he had not heard, the secondary sense made visible.
The source section describes turning away by refusing to listen or comply; this ayah depicts someone who hears God's signs, then persists arrogantly as if he had not heard, and warns of punishment.

The source section connects turning away with leaving attentive listening; here disbelievers tell one another not to listen to the Quran and to make noise over it, an explicit effort to block hearing.

The source section joins the Prophet's limited responsibility for guidance to people who turn away; this ayah says if they turn away, his duty is only clear delivery, repeating that limit in the context of refusal.

The source section describes the turn-away person alongside a caller to heed; this ayah tells the Messenger to remind, and 88:22-23 clarify that he cannot control people who then turn away and disbelieve.
The source section says guidance is not the Prophet's responsibility; this ayah states he is not set over people as a controller, immediately before 88:23 names those who turn away and disbelieve.
The source section pairs denial with turning away and develops an animal image for the denier; this ayah asks why people turn away from the reminder, before 74:50-51 compare them to fleeing donkeys.

The source section's dictionary sense for ك ذ ب/B007 describes a wild animal running and looking back; this ayah compares people turning from the reminder to alarmed donkeys, a specific fleeing-animal parallel, though it does not show the source's backward glance.

The source section's dictionary sense for ك ذ ب/B007 uses a wild animal running before it stops to look back; this ayah says the donkeys flee from a lion, echoing flight from a threat but not the pause or backward look.
